entries.headline: Falcon Energy Materials agrees to pay US$22 million for a Chinese graphite stake
entries.dek: The deal gives the TSX Venture-listed company a 49% stake in a profitable anode-material producer in Shandong province, funded by a private placement closed in September.
entries.caption: An industrial materials processing facility, illustrative; Tuesday's deal centres on a Chinese graphite anode producer that supplies battery manufacturers.

sources.title: Falcon Energy Materials PLC Announces Landmark Acquisition of 49% Strategic Interest in Established Graphite Anode Producer

unverified_claims: Weihai's profitability and the terms of its long-term supply contracts rest solely on Falcon's own announcement and have not been independently verified.
Falcon's characterization of the deal as 'a defining milestone' is the company's own assessment.
brief: Falcon Energy Materials plc (TSX-V: FLCN; OTCQB: FLCNF), through its wholly owned subsidiary Falcon EMG Holdings Ltd, has agreed to acquire a 49% non-operating equity interest in Weihai Hensen New Materials Technology Co., Ltd., a Chinese producer of natural flake and synthetic graphite anode materials, for US$22 million in cash.

Weihai operates a 25,000-tonne-per-year production facility in Shandong province and has been profitable since starting commercial output in the second half of 2025, selling under long-term contracts to Chinese anode manufacturers. Falcon says the purchase is fully funded by a C$34-million placement closed September 23, and expects to close by year-end, pending Chinese regulatory approvals.

Under a shareholder agreement, Falcon will have the right to nominate a director, veto power over key decisions requiring unanimous approval, and rights of first offer or refusal on Weihai's shares. CEO Matthieu Bos called the acquisition 'a defining milestone for Falcon.'
body: Falcon Energy Materials plc (TSX-V: FLCN; OTCQB: FLCNF) has agreed to acquire a 49% strategic, non-operating equity interest in Weihai Hensen New Materials Technology Co., Ltd., a Chinese producer of natural flake graphite and synthetic graphite anode materials, for US$22 million in cash. The transaction is being carried out through Falcon EMG Holdings Ltd, a wholly owned Falcon subsidiary, under an Equity Transfer Agreement with Weihai's sole equity holder.

Weihai is based in Shandong province and operates a production facility with capacity for 25,000 tonnes a year of coated spheronized purified graphite, or CSPG, a processed anode material. Founded in 2023, the company began commercial production in the second half of 2025. Falcon's announcement describes Weihai as profitable, selling its output under long-term contracts to leading Chinese anode material manufacturers.

Falcon describes the acquisition as a step in its strategy to become, in its own words, 'an integrated, global supplier of critical battery materials.' The 49% stake is structured as non-operating, so Falcon will not run Weihai's daily operations, but a shareholder agreement gives Falcon the right to nominate a director, a requirement that key decisions receive unanimous board approval, and rights of first offer and first refusal over Weihai's remaining equity.

Falcon said the purchase is fully funded from a C$34-million non-brokered private placement that it closed on September 23, 2026. A non-brokered placement is one sold directly to investors without an underwriting syndicate acting as agent.

The acquisition itself is expected to close by the end of the fourth quarter of 2026, subject to Chinese regulatory approvals, including registrations with the State Administration for Market Regulation and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange, as well as other customary closing conditions.

Falcon chief executive Matthieu Bos said the acquisition is 'a defining milestone for Falcon,' calling it the execution of commitments the company had previously made to its shareholders regarding its battery-materials strategy. Falcon's shares trade on the TSX Venture Exchange under the symbol FLCN and on the OTCQB marketplace under FLCNF.

entries.headline: Salesforce agrees to buy voice-AI startup Cresta in a deal reported at $2.7 billion
entries.dek: The company has not disclosed terms; Cresta's voice agents already serve Marriott, Comcast and Alaska Airlines, and the deal should close early in fiscal 2028.
entries.caption: A customer-service call centre sits dim and quiet, illustrative of the voice-automation technology at the centre of Tuesday's acquisition.

sources.title: Salesforce Signs Definitive Agreement to Acquire Cresta
DMG BLOCKCHAIN SOLUTIONS INC (TSXV: DMGI) quote, -11.54% on about $67,827
NEPTUNE DIGITAL ASSETS CORP (TSXV: NDA) quote, -2.08% on about $30,181

unverified_claims: The $2.7 billion purchase price is reported by The Information; Salesforce's own announcement does not state a price.
brief: Salesforce has signed a definitive agreement to acquire Cresta, an artificial intelligence company whose voice agents handle customer service calls and coach human representatives in real time. Salesforce's own announcement names no purchase price; The Information has reported the deal at approximately $2.7 billion. Cresta already serves Marriott, Comcast and Alaska Airlines.

The acquisition pairs Cresta's voice technology with Salesforce's Service Cloud and Agentforce products, extending the company's customer-service push from chat into phone calls. Kishan Chetan, who leads Agentforce and Service Cloud, said voice is 'where service is hardest to get right.' The deal is expected to close in the first quarter of Salesforce's 2028 fiscal year, subject to regulatory approval.

Away from Salesforce, the venture board's digital assets theme comprises 14 listed names; four traded today, one higher and two lower, for a median move of -1.04% against -0.37% for the S&P/TSX Venture Composite. Dmg Blockchain Solutions Inc (TSXV: DMGI) fell 11.54% to CAD0.345, and is in the theme because its registered name contains "blockchain." Nothing connects the two.
body: Salesforce has signed a definitive agreement to acquire Cresta, an artificial intelligence company whose voice agents handle customer service calls end-to-end and coach human representatives in real time. Salesforce's own announcement does not state a purchase price; The Information has reported the deal at approximately $2.7 billion. Cresta already serves enterprise clients including Marriott, Comcast and Alaska Airlines.

The acquisition is intended to pair Cresta's voice technology with Salesforce's Service Cloud and Agentforce products, extending the company's customer-service push from text and chat into phone calls. Kishan Chetan, who leads Agentforce and Service Cloud for Salesforce, said in the announcement that voice is 'where service is hardest to get right, and where it matters most to customers.'

Cresta chief executive Ping Wu said the combination will help 'turn every customer interaction into a competitive advantage' by building real-time conversation intelligence directly into Salesforce's service platform. Salesforce said Cresta will continue to support the contact-centre and telephony platforms its customers currently use after the deal closes.

The deal is expected to close in the first quarter of Salesforce's 2028 fiscal year, subject to regulatory approval and other customary closing conditions, the companies said. Neither company's announcement discloses the terms of the transaction beyond the expected timing, and the $2.7-billion figure circulating in media reports has not been confirmed by either party.

On the venture boards, the digital assets theme comprises 14 listed venture names; 4 traded today, 1 higher and 2 lower, for a median move of -1.04% against -0.37% for the S&P/TSX Venture Composite, a spread of -0.67 percentage points.

Dmg Blockchain Solutions Inc (TSXV: DMGI) fell 11.54% to CAD0.345, and is in the theme because its registered name contains "blockchain." Neptune Digital Assets Corp (TSXV: NDA) fell 2.08% to CAD0.47, and is in the theme because its registered name contains "digital asset." The moves and Salesforce's announcement fall on the same day; nothing in either company's disclosure connects the two.

entries.headline: Standard Uranium boosts its flow-through placement to $2 million
entries.dek: Strong demand led the Saskatchewan-focused explorer to increase the non-brokered offering to 25 million units at $0.08, with warrants exercisable at $0.12.
entries.caption: A flow-through placement for Standard Uranium's Saskatchewan projects grew to $2 million on what the company called strong demand.
unverified_claims: The company's characterization of 'strong demand' driving the upsize is the company's own stated reason.
No closing date is given; completion remains subject to TSX Venture Exchange acceptance.
brief: Standard Uranium Ltd. (TSXV: STND) has increased the size of its previously announced non-brokered private placement, citing strong demand. The company will now offer up to 25 million flow-through units at $0.08 each, for gross proceeds of up to $2 million.

Each unit includes one flow-through common share and half a warrant; each whole warrant allows the holder to buy one additional common share at $0.12, exercisable starting 61 days after closing and expiring 24 months later. The company said net proceeds will fund exploration of its Saskatchewan uranium projects.

The offering carries no resale hold period under Canadian securities law and remains subject to TSX Venture Exchange approval; the release does not give a closing date. Finders may receive fees for introducing eligible subscribers to the offering.
body: Standard Uranium Ltd. (TSXV: STND, OTCQB: STTDF) has increased the size of a previously announced private placement, citing strong investor demand. The non-brokered offering, conducted under the listed issuer financing exemption in National Instrument 45-106, will now raise up to $2 million through the sale of as many as 25 million flow-through units priced at $0.08 each.

Each flow-through unit consists of one common share, issued under the flow-through provisions of the Income Tax Act, and one half of a common share purchase warrant. A whole warrant entitles its holder to buy one additional common share at $0.12, with the right to exercise beginning 61 days after closing and running until 24 months after that date.

A flow-through share lets the issuer renounce the associated tax deductions to the subscriber rather than claiming them itself, which is why flow-through financings are priced at a premium and used specifically to fund Canadian exploration spending. Standard Uranium said the net proceeds from this offering will go toward exploring its Saskatchewan uranium projects.

The release states the securities issued will not be subject to a resale hold period under applicable Canadian securities laws. Completion remains subject to acceptance by the TSX Venture Exchange, and finder's fees are payable to eligible parties who introduce subscribers to the offering, though no rate or specific finder is named.

The release does not give a closing date for the offering, and it does not state the size of the previously announced placement that this increase replaces, so the scale of today's upsizing cannot be measured against the original offer. Standard Uranium has not named a specific lead or sole finder in the release.

entries.headline: Aether Global pushes InMotion Energy deal deadline three weeks to Nov. 21
entries.dek: The defence-and-security technology company and clean-energy fleet firm InMotion now have until November 21 to sign a definitive agreement under their proposed business combination.
entries.caption: Aether Global and InMotion Energy now have until November 21 to sign a definitive combination agreement.

sources.title: Aether Global Innovations Announces Extension of Letter of Intent with InMotion Energy Corp.

unverified_claims: The release does not disclose financial terms, an exchange ratio, or a valuation for the proposed business combination.
There is no assurance stated in the release that the transaction will be completed by the new deadline or at all.
brief: Aether Global Innovations Corp. (CSE: AETH), a defence and security technology company, has extended the exclusivity period and term of its letter of intent with InMotion Energy Corp. by three weeks, to November 21 from October 31. All other terms of the original LOI remain unchanged, the company said.

The proposed combination would bring together Aether's unmanned-systems and counter-drone business with InMotion, a clean-energy company developing solar power systems for transportation fleets. The deal is classified as a "Fundamental Change" under Canadian Securities Exchange policy and would require a definitive agreement, shareholder approval and CSE approval before it could complete.

The original letter of intent was signed September 28. The companies said they continue to work toward finalizing and executing a definitive agreement by the new deadline, with no assurance the transaction will ultimately be completed.
body: Aether Global Innovations Corp. (CSE: AETH, OTC: AETHF), a defence and security technology company, has extended the exclusivity period and term of its binding letter of intent with InMotion Energy Corp. by three weeks, moving the deadline to November 21 from October 31. The company said all other terms of the original LOI, first signed September 28, remain unchanged.

The proposed transaction would combine Aether's unmanned-systems and counter-drone business with InMotion, which operates through its subsidiary Deecell Inc. developing solar power systems for transportation fleets. Aether described the pairing as a proposed business combination between the two companies, which the release classifies as a "Fundamental Change" under Canadian Securities Exchange policy.

Completing the deal requires the parties to execute a definitive agreement, obtain shareholder approval, and secure CSE approval, none of which have yet occurred. The companies said they continue to work toward finalizing those steps by the new November 21 deadline, and the release states there is no assurance the transaction will be completed.

The announcement does not disclose financial terms for the proposed combination, an exchange ratio, or a valuation for either company. Both Aether and InMotion remain separately listed companies while the parties negotiate toward a definitive agreement, and the release gives no specifics beyond the extended timeline and the classification of the deal as a Fundamental Change.

Today's release is itself short: it extends one deadline and confirms no other term has moved. Readers following either company should expect the next disclosure to be either a definitive agreement or confirmation that the proposed combination has lapsed at the new November 21 deadline.

entries.headline: A SpaceX-Tesla merger could hand Musk 56% voting control
entries.dek: Barclays estimates the combination would give Musk roughly 37% ownership of the combined company, without triggering the $1-trillion Tesla pay package shareholders approved.
entries.caption: An empty boardroom at Tesla's scale of ambition: voting control, not cash, is what a SpaceX combination would actually hand Musk.

sources.title: Musk's pay under a SpaceX-Tesla merger: voting control, but no $1 trillion payday

unverified_claims: Barclays' estimates of Musk's post-merger ownership (~37%) and voting power (~56%) are analyst projections about a hypothetical transaction, not a confirmed deal or company disclosure.
There is no confirmed SpaceX-Tesla merger; the analysis describes what voting control would look like under one.
brief: A SpaceX-Tesla merger would give Elon Musk about 56% of the combined company's voting power, Barclays analysts estimate, versus the roughly 29% he would hold even if he meets every milestone under the $1-trillion Tesla pay package shareholders already approved, Reuters reported.

SpaceX's own compensation plan hands Musk 85% voting control immediately, without operational milestones, with the stock's value tied to targets including Mars colonization and data-center buildouts worth up to $719 billion at the highest level. Tesla's $2-trillion market-cap threshold for any merger-linked award compares with its current $1.6-trillion valuation.

On the venture boards, the space theme comprises two listed names; of those, none cleared the C$25,000 daily-volume threshold this bulletin uses to call a price change a trade, so none is named here. The S&P/TSX Venture Composite fell 0.37% on the day.
body: A merger between SpaceX and Tesla could hand Elon Musk substantially more control over the combined company than the $1-trillion pay package Tesla shareholders approved last year, Reuters reported. Barclays analysts estimate that in a merger, Musk would own roughly 37% of the combined entity but hold about 56% of its voting power, a figure well above the roughly 29% voting control the Tesla package alone would eventually give him if every milestone is met.

The difference comes from how the two pay structures are built. Tesla's package requires Musk to hit a series of market-capitalization and operational milestones before any additional stock, and the voting power that comes with it, is released. SpaceX's own compensation plan, approved separately, gives Musk 85% voting control from the outset, with no operational conditions attached, because of a special class of shares that carries ten votes each.

SpaceX's stock-based incentives are themselves tied to ambitious targets — Mars colonization, data-center expansion, and further market-capitalization goals — that could be worth as much as $719 billion at the highest tier, according to the reporting. Under a merger scenario, any additional Tesla-linked award would not trigger until the combined company's market capitalization reached $2 trillion, versus Tesla's current standalone valuation of about $1.6 trillion; reaching that threshold would issue Musk $20 billion in shares.

Governance observers quoted in the reporting were skeptical that the pay structure itself was the real story. Corporate governance expert Charles Elson called the package "a distraction from the real story, which is complete control." Accounting professor Matthew Bloomfield described the SpaceX plan as "just a marketing document," saying Musk includes ambitious targets to "get a bunch of people hyped."

SpaceX completed its initial public offering in the summer of 2026, and the merger itself remains speculative — there is no confirmed transaction, only analysis of what one could look like under the two companies' existing pay structures. The $1-trillion Tesla package approved by shareholders last year was structured around milestones Musk had not yet met at the time of the reporting.

On the venture boards, the space theme — two listed names — saw muted activity on the day: one showed a print, but neither cleared the C$25,000 daily-volume floor this bulletin requires before naming a price change a trade, so neither is identified here. The S&P/TSX Venture Composite, the benchmark against which this bulletin measures small-cap moves, fell 0.37% over the same session.
